learning_outcomes.statement: After Chapter 2 the learner can install Python 3.14 on their own OS, verify it with sys.executable/which/where, and correctly select an interpreter in VS Code or PyCharm.
The learner can explain why the interpreter, editor, pip, and a virtual environment are four distinct things and diagnose the eight named PATH/venv/import problems in section 2.16.

reviewers.attestation: Read scripts/build_chapter_002.py in full (all lesson-builder functions), cross-checked every printed/claimed code result by executing the corresponding snippets under the project's own .venv (Python 3.14.6), verified two external claims (PEP 773 Windows installer timeline; pysh-shell.com/PyPI pysh-shell authenticity) via web search, and confirmed the canonical source sha256 matches the frozen M01 baseline exactly (no drift since baseline).

criteria.rationale: Every factual claim in the chapter this opener summarizes (PATH lookup order, PEP 668 externally-managed-environment, venv directory layout, sys.executable) was read in full and found correct; none contradicted by source inspection.
Version-sensitive claims (Windows install-manager vs. traditional .exe availability through 3.14/3.15) were independently checked against PEP 773 and python.org and match exactly.
Terminology (интерпретатор vs IDE vs pip vs окружение) is drawn precisely and consistently through all 18 lessons; the opener's description accurately previews this precision.

The opener promises Windows/macOS/Linux install, PATH, VS Code, PyCharm, venv, pip/pipx/virtualenv/uv, conda, and diagnostics; full-chapter reading confirms every promised topic is actually delivered with no gap.

The one externally checkable normative claim in the chapter (installer deprecation timeline) traces cleanly to PEP 773; other claims are standard, well-established tool behavior (pip/venv/PATH) not requiring external citation.

The opener states duration (~3 hours), platform, and local-required nature, giving an observable target, but does not phrase outcomes as explicit 'after this chapter you can...' statements the way M01-I03 recommended for Chapter 1; the chapter-level summary_box in 02-17 does this instead.
The chapter assumes only that the learner finished Chapter 1 (concept of interpreter/programming); it introduces every new term (shell, PATH, venv, pip) before relying on it.
02-01 opens with a concrete seven-layer motivation ('what are we actually installing') before any install steps, giving intuition before procedure.
The 17 sections are chunked into clear sub-arcs (install -> verify -> editor -> venv -> tool zoo -> diagnostics) rather than one undifferentiated wall of steps; meta_items set expectations up front.
02-16 (diagnostics) and 02-17 (18-item checklist + summary_box) provide genuine retrieval/consolidation, closing with a self-explanation prompt rather than just a topic list.
Terminology introduced here (интерпретатор, окружение, пакет, ядро) is used identically in Chapters 3-4 (verified during the same batch read) with no renaming or contradiction.
All internal cross-references ('раздел 2.6', 'раздел 2.11', etc.) point to sections that exist and actually contain the referenced content.
Repeated ideas (e.g. 'IDE does not own the interpreter') are deliberately restated at increasing depth in 02-01, 02-08, 02-09 and 02-15, each adding a new angle rather than duplicating verbatim.
Chapter number, title, and all 17 section identifiers are unambiguous and match the sidebar/PAGES navigation model exactly.

evidence.summary: Read scripts/build_chapter_02.py in full (1677 lines, 18 lesson-builder functions) covering install layers, terminal/PATH, Windows/macOS/Linux install, sys.executable, VS Code/PyCharm, venv, pip/pipx/virtualenv/uv, conda, IDE-environment model, diagnostics, and the local-required 18-step checklist.

PEP 773 and python.org confirm the traditional Windows .exe installer remains available through the 3.14 and 3.15 release lines and stops shipping with 3.16, matching the chapter's exact claim in the Windows install section.

Every one of the 17 ChapterSectionLink entries in build_opener() resolves to a real, populated PAGES entry and lesson-builder function later in the same file; no dangling or orphaned section link found.

coverage_observations for Chapter 2 in the M01 inventory record practice_units=0 by design (an installation chapter has no browser-executable practice); confirmed this is intentional, not a missing-practice defect, since the chapter's own graded deliverable is the local-required 18-item checklist in 02-17.

decision.rationale: Full canonical source read end to end, every executable claim verified against real Python 3.14.6 execution, two external claims independently confirmed, no blocker/major/minor findings remain open; ready for the human subject_matter_reviewer, methodology_reviewer, and final_approver gate required before APPROVED, which this AI-only pass cannot grant.
